note: Topic pool for the Quill-genre prompt family, written 2026-10-23 before any generation for this experiment. prompts.py assigns dev / eval / reserve by seeded draw (plan.md section 4); nothing here is chosen after seeing outputs. Instructions read the way writers type into Quill: the task plus their own points. Facts beyond common knowledge are left to the writer, as the drafting prompt requires.

argument.evidence: the writer's points only; no outside statistics

topics.instructions: Argue that our district should NOT switch to a four-day school week. My points: kids who need school meals lose a day of food, working parents would have to pay for a fifth day of childcare, and longer school days are exhausting for younger kids.

Argue that elementary schools should get rid of graded homework. Points: little kids learn more from playing and reading for fun, homework mostly measures how much help a kid gets at home, and families fight about it every night.
Argue for letting 16-year-olds vote in local elections. Points: they already work and pay sales tax, school board decisions affect them most, and people who vote young tend to keep voting.
Argue that colleges should pay their athletes directly. Points: the players bring in the money, practice is basically a full-time job, and a scholarship doesn't cover everything an athlete needs.

Argue for a year-round calendar with shorter breaks spread out. Points: kids forget a lot over a long summer, shorter breaks mean less review in the fall, and families could take vacations outside the busy season.

personal.evidence: the writer's own experience; details the writer didn't give should be bracketed placeholders

topics.instructions: Write about learning to swim when I was 13, way later than my friends. I was embarrassed to be in the class with little kids. The instructor let me practice before the others came. By the end of summer I could swim a full lap.

Write about moving from the city to a small town in 7th grade. I hated how quiet it was at first. A neighbor taught me to fix bikes and that's how I made friends. Now I like that everyone knows each other.

Write about my grandmother's dumpling recipe that she never wrote down. I watched her make them every New Year. After she got sick I tried to make them from memory and failed three times. The fourth time my mom said they tasted right.
Write about deciding to quit piano after eight years. My parents were disappointed. I felt guilty but I wasn't enjoying it. I started playing again on my own two years later, just songs I liked.

topics.topic: first job at a grocery store
topics.instructions: Write about my first job bagging groceries. The first week I was too slow and a customer yelled at me. An older coworker showed me how to pack heavy things first. I learned to stay calm when people are rude.

literary.evidence: the work itself; no invented quotations

topics.topic: the conch in Lord of the Flies
topics.instructions: Analyze what the conch shell stands for in Lord of the Flies. My points: at first it means order and everyone gets a turn to speak, the boys stop respecting it as things fall apart, and when it's destroyed the last bit of civilization goes with it.

topics.topic: Boo Radley in To Kill a Mockingbird
topics.instructions: Analyze how Boo Radley changes in the kids' eyes in To Kill a Mockingbird. Points: they start out treating him like a monster from a story, the gifts in the tree show he's watching out for them, and in the end Scout understands him as a person.

Analyze whether fate or the characters' own choices cause the ending of Romeo and Juliet. My view: the prologue says they're doomed, but the rushed decisions, like the secret marriage and Romeo killing Tybalt, are what actually make it happen.

Analyze the ending of The Giver and why it's left open. Points: we don't know if Jonas and Gabe survive, the music and lights could be real or a dying dream, and the uncertainty matches the book's theme about choice and feeling.

topics.topic: the house in The House on Mango Street
topics.instructions: Analyze what the house means to Esperanza in The House on Mango Street. Points: it's not the house her parents promised, she's ashamed of it, and by the end she realizes she'll leave but come back for the people who can't.

explanation.evidence: widely established facts only, stated no more precisely than common knowledge

topics.instructions: Explain why ocean tides go in and out. Cover the moon's pull, why there are two high tides a day, and why some tides are bigger than others.

topics.topic: how a bill becomes a law
topics.instructions: Explain how a bill becomes a federal law in the US. Cover introducing it, committees, both houses voting, and the president signing or vetoing.
Explain why we add a leap day to the calendar. Cover how long a year really is, what would happen to the seasons without it, and the rule about century years.
Explain what a credit score is and why it matters when you're starting out. Cover what raises and lowers it in general terms and why paying on time matters most.

topics.topic: how vaccines train the immune system
topics.instructions: Explain how vaccines help the body fight disease. Cover what the immune system remembers, what a vaccine shows it, and why some vaccines need boosters.

Compare reading e-books and printed books. My points: e-books are cheaper and easier to carry, printed books are easier on the eyes and you remember them better, and it depends on what you're reading.
Compare growing up in a city and in the country. Points: cities have more to do and better public transport, the country has more space and less noise, and both can be lonely in different ways.
Compare playing team sports and individual sports. Points: team sports teach you to rely on others, individual sports put all the pressure on you, and both teach discipline.
Compare texting and calling. Points: texting lets you think before you answer, calls are faster for anything complicated, and tone gets lost in texts.

Compare going to a public university and a private college. Points: public is usually cheaper for in-state students, private often has smaller classes, and financial aid can flip which one costs less.

cause.evidence: the writer's points only; no invented statistics

topics.topic: effects of not getting enough sleep
topics.instructions: Write about what happens when teenagers don't get enough sleep. Causes: phones in bed, early start times, too much homework. Effects: trouble focusing, bad moods, getting sick more.

topics.topic: why small towns lose young people
topics.instructions: Write about why young people leave small towns. Causes: few jobs, no college nearby, not much to do. Effects: aging population, schools closing, local businesses struggling.
Write about the effects of fast fashion. Causes: cheap prices, trends changing every few weeks. Effects: clothes thrown away quickly, pollution from factories, low pay for workers.
Write about why people put things off. Causes: fear of doing it badly, tasks that feel too big, distractions that feel better right now. Effects: stress, rushed work, missed deadlines.

topics.topic: effects of a new highway on a town
topics.instructions: Write about what happens to a small town when a highway bypasses it. Causes: traffic no longer goes through main street. Effects: gas stations and diners close, but the town gets quieter and safer.

topics.topic: letter asking the city for a crosswalk
topics.instructions: Write a letter asking the city council to add a crosswalk on Maple Street by the elementary school. Points: kids cross between parked cars, drivers go fast on that stretch, and there was a near miss last month.

topics.topic: letter to the principal about lunch time
topics.instructions: Write a letter asking for a longer lunch period. Points: 25 minutes isn't enough when the line takes 10, kids skip eating, and afternoon classes suffer.

topics.topic: letter to a landlord about repairs
topics.instructions: Write a letter to my landlord asking him to fix the heating. Points: it's been broken for two weeks, I reported it twice, and the lease says he's responsible.

topics.topic: letter to the editor about the library
topics.instructions: Write a letter to the editor opposing cuts to the library's hours. Points: it's the only free place to study, people use the computers for job applications, and the savings are small.

topics.topic: letter to a coach asking to switch positions
topics.instructions: Write a letter to my coach asking to try playing defense instead of forward. Points: I read the game well, I'm better at tackling than shooting, and the team is short on defenders.

review.evidence: the writer's own opinions; no invented specifics about the product

topics.instructions: Write a review of our school cafeteria. My opinions: the pizza is good, the salad bar is usually wilted, prices went up this year, and the new seating is better.
Write a review of Riverside Park. My opinions: great trails and the playground is new, the bathrooms are always locked, and parking fills up on weekends.

topics.topic: review of an online study app
topics.instructions: Write a review of the flashcard app our class uses. My opinions: making cards is fast, the spaced repetition actually helps, but the free version has too many ads.
Write a review of the bakery on Main Street. My opinions: the croissants are the best in town, the line is long in the morning, and the staff remember regulars.

topics.topic: review of a museum field trip
topics.instructions: Write a review of our field trip to the science museum. My opinions: the planetarium show was the highlight, the exhibits were too crowded with school groups, and we didn't have enough time.

topics.topic: how to study for a big test
topics.instructions: Write a how-to about studying for a big test. My tips: start a week early, quiz yourself instead of rereading, sleep the night before, and study in short blocks.

topics.topic: how to start a vegetable garden
topics.instructions: Write a how-to about starting a small vegetable garden. My tips: pick a sunny spot, start with easy plants like lettuce and beans, water in the morning, and don't plant too much at once.
Write a how-to about making a simple budget. My tips: write down what you earn, track spending for a month, set aside savings first, and leave some money for fun.

topics.topic: how to give a class presentation
topics.instructions: Write a how-to about giving a presentation in class. My tips: practice out loud, use notes not a script, look at a few friendly faces, and it's fine to pause.

topics.topic: how to train a dog to sit
topics.instructions: Write a how-to about teaching a puppy to sit. My tips: use small treats, keep sessions short, say the word once, and reward right away.

application.evidence: the writer's own experience; details not given should be bracketed placeholders

topics.topic: college essay about running a food drive
topics.instructions: Write my college application essay about organizing a food drive at my school. We collected way more than expected. The hardest part was getting people to volunteer. It made me want to study public health.
Write a scholarship essay about why I want to become a teacher. I tutor younger kids after school. One student went from failing to passing math. I want to teach in the district I grew up in.

topics.topic: job application for a library assistant
topics.instructions: Write my application essay for a part-time library assistant job. I volunteer at the library already. I'm organized and good with computers. I like helping older people with technology.
Write my application for a summer engineering program. I built a small robot from a kit and then redesigned it. I'm in the robotics club. I want to learn how real engineers test designs.

Write my transfer essay for moving from community college to a four-year university. I started at community college to save money. I found I love biology through a lab class. I want research opportunities my college doesn't have.

blog.evidence: the writer's own views and experience

topics.topic: trying a month without buying anything new
topics.instructions: Write a blog post about my month of not buying anything new. The first week was hard. I found I mostly shopped when bored. I saved money and kept the habit partly.

topics.topic: why I started walking to school
topics.instructions: Write a blog post about why I started walking to school instead of getting a ride. It takes 25 minutes. I listen to podcasts. I feel more awake in first period.
Write a blog post about teaching myself to cook from online videos. I started with eggs and pasta. I burned a lot of things. Now I make dinner for my family twice a week.

topics.topic: deleting a game I was addicted to
topics.instructions: Write a blog post about deleting a phone game I played for hours every day. I didn't notice how much time it took. The first days I kept reaching for my phone. I read two books that month.
Write a blog post about volunteering at the animal shelter on weekends. I mostly clean and walk dogs. Some dogs are scared of everyone at first. Seeing one get adopted is the best part.

position.evidence: reasoning from the writer's points; no invented studies or quotes

topics.instructions: Write a position paper on whether zoos should exist. My position: good zoos should stay because they protect endangered species and teach kids, but roadside zoos should be shut down.

Write a position paper arguing that high schools should require a personal finance class. Points: many adults never learned about debt or taxes, it's more useful than some required classes, and parents can't always teach it.

topics.topic: is it ethical to eat meat
topics.instructions: Write a position paper on whether eating meat is ethical. My position: it's hard to defend factory farming, but eating meat from animals raised humanely can be justified.

topics.topic: should social media require age verification
topics.instructions: Write a position paper on requiring age checks for social media. My position: I support it for kids under 13, but worry about privacy if everyone has to upload an ID.
Write a position paper on banning cars from downtown areas. My position: car-free streets on weekends are a good start, but a full ban hurts people with disabilities and delivery businesses.
